planting.note: Plant bare-root fans or container divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun; Sunday Gloves holds its pale color best where it gets some relief from the hottest afternoon sun.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, and water deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Sunday Gloves bears large, loosely ruffled, near-white flowers with a pale yellow eye and a tiny celery-green throat, carried on scapes to about 30 inches; the sweetly fragrant blooms are especially noticeable in the evening. It flowers from early to late summer with a dependable rebloom flush. Deadhead spent scapes to tidy the planting and divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to maintain vigorous flowering.

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Celestial Eyes is a semi-evergreen tetraploid, so gardeners in colder zones should expect more winter dieback than with dormant cultivars.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Celestial Eyes bears six-inch flowers blending cream, peach, and pink tones around a striking slate-violet eye and a matching picotee edge above a green throat, carried on scapes around two feet tall with heavy branching and high bud counts for a long early-midseason display with dependable rebloom. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Rapid Eye Movement Daylily (Yellow Daylily with Maroon Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this evergreen tetraploid performs best where winters are not extremely harsh.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Rapid Eye Movement bears large, clear bright-yellow flowers nearly seven inches across, marked with a bold, dark maroon eye and matching edge above a green-yellow throat, carried on scapes around 32 inches tall. It received an AHS Honorable Mention for its striking color contrast and garden performance. This evergreen tetraploid blooms in early midseason and reblooms through summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Open My Eyes Daylily (Orange Daylily with Purple Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; the evergreen foliage of Open My Eyes performs best in regions without extended hard freezes.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Open My Eyes bears orange flowers just over five inches across with a dark purple eye above a distinctive green heart-shaped throat, carried on scapes around two feet tall. This evergreen tetraploid blooms in an early-to-midseason flush and shows minimal flower-slicking even in full sun. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Eye of Newt Daylily (Compact Gold Daylily with Black-Purple Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; the compact habit of Eye of Newt suits front-of-border placement.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Eye of Newt bears compact, three-inch, yellow-gold flowers with a large, bold purple-black eyezone above a green throat, held on scapes only about 18 inches tall above tidy, semi-evergreen foliage. This diploid blooms in a mid-to-late season flush and reblooms. Its small scale suits edging and mixed containers. Divide congested clumps every few years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Edge of Darkness Daylily (Lavender Daylily with Purple Picotee Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Edge of Darkness is evergreen, so it performs best where winters are not severely cold.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Edge of Darkness bears fragrant, five-inch lavender flowers marked with a strong dark-purple eyezone and a matching picotee edge above a yellow throat, carried on scapes about 25 inches tall. This evergreen tetraploid blooms in early midseason and reblooms, and received an AHS Honorable Mention for its crisp, well-defined pattern. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Strawberry Fields Forever Daylily (Pink Daylily with Strawberry-Rose Eye)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this evergreen, fragrant tetraploid rewards deadheading to keep the planting tidy through its long bloom season.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Strawberry Fields Forever bears fragrant, soft pink flowers with a fringed edge and a deeper strawberry-rose eyezone and edge above a chartreuse-green throat, carried on scapes around 26 inches tall. This evergreen tetraploid blooms from early-midseason into summer with dependable rebloom. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Hot Buttered Rum Daylily (Tall Late-Season Orange Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; site Hot Buttered Rum toward the back of the border, where its height and late timing extend the daylily season after earlier cultivars fade.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Hot Buttered Rum bears soft orange flowers about six inches across with yellow midribs and ruffled yellow edges above a yellow-to-green throat, carried on tall scapes reaching about 40 inches. This dormant tetraploid is notably late-blooming, getting underway as many earlier daylilies are finishing, and reblooms into the fall. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Sonoran Desert Rose Daylily (Tall Late-Season Red Bitone Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Sonoran Desert Rose is a vigorous, heavily branched grower that benefits from extra spacing as clumps mature.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Sonoran Desert Rose bears light red bitone flowers about six and a half inches across with a more intensely colored eye and some gold edging, with striping that varies somewhat from bloom to bloom, carried on heavily branched scapes to about 40 inches. This dormant tetraploid is a late bloomer that extends the daylily season well into late summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Golden Glitz Daylily (Tall Late-Season Golden Yellow Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Golden Glitz's tall, heavily branched scapes benefit from a sheltered spot out of strong wind.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Golden Glitz bears rich golden-yellow flowers about seven inches across with a small green throat and rolled-back sepals that give each bloom a triangular shape, carried on scapes to roughly 42 inches with heavy five-way branching and high bud counts. This dormant tetraploid flowers late in the season, extending color into late summer. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Last Chance for Love Daylily (Tall Late-Season Rose Pink Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; as its name suggests, Last Chance for Love is valued for carrying the daylily display into the very end of the season.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Last Chance for Love bears rose-pink flowers about six inches across with white midribs, a darker rose band, a cream edge on the sepals, and a yellow-to-green throat, with striping that varies somewhat from day to day, carried on tall scapes to about 42 inches with heavy five-way branching. This dormant tetraploid is a notably late bloomer that reblooms. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.

common_name: Cactus Blossom Daylily (Tall Late-Season Strawberry-Edged Daylily)

planting.note: Plant divisions in spring or fall in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; Cactus Blossom's heavily branched, late-season scapes benefit from extra spacing as clumps mature.

directions: Plant divisions with the crown about an inch below soil level in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun, watering deeply through the first season to establish a strong root system. Cactus Blossom bears strawberry-colored flowers about five and a quarter inches across with a strawberry-and-gold toothy edge above a yellow-green throat, carried on scapes to about 41 inches with heavy five-way branching and roughly two dozen buds per scape. This dormant tetraploid is a late bloomer that extends color into the end of the daylily season. Divide congested clumps every three to four years in spring to sustain vigorous flowering.
